dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between shallow and deep when folded at 14.6 days (odd vs even difference at 6 sigma) and the individual transits have inconsistent depths, which is expected if the true period is twice as long and the signal is from a binary. A planet would have the same depth each time. The long duration for this small M-dwarf and blend indicators support a blended binary rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ at 6 sigma with 6650 ppm difference — strong evidence the 14.6 d period is the half-period of an eclipsing binary at 29.2 d, not a planet at 14.6 d. sector_oe_max_sigma 5.184 and sector_oe_sectors_over_3 2 on same sign.

Inconsistent transits: one is -4.2 sigma shallow (2305 ppm) and one +4.0 sigma deep (12162 ppm) with top 3 carrying 0.98 of the signal. A planet should have consistent depths; this matches variable eclipses / noise.
Independent planet scorer ranks this in the low-planet-likelihood tail, consistent with blend/false-alarm similar cases.

Transit is too long for a central transit of this M dwarf (TIC rad 0.398, Gaia FLAME 0.446 rad), and combined with odd/even and inconsistent depths the flat shape (v_sigma -2.326) does not outweigh the EB indicators; a blended eclipsing binary can also be flat-bottomed.
